chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who died and made a bequest that Hajj be performed on his behalf. He said: 'If it is a compulsory (Fard) Hajj, it is taken from all the wealth; and if it is a voluntary (Nafl) Hajj, it is taken from one-third of his wealth.'

key_terms.صَرُورَةً: Compulsory or obligatory (referring to Fard Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the source of funds for Hajj performed on behalf of a deceased person?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the Hajj al-Din (obligatory debt) and Hajj al-Tatawwu (voluntary), ruling that the former is paid from the entire estate while the latter is limited to one-third, mirroring the general inheritance rules for bequests. This distinction highlights the juristic view that the obligatory Hajj is a debt upon the deceased's soul, whereas the voluntary act is a recommended deed that does not carry the same priority in estate distribution. The ruling underscores the importance of fulfilling religious obligations before executing voluntary wishes in Islamic inheritance law.
